## Arithmetic sequences {#ss3-definition .ap-lesson}

An **arithmetic sequence**, or **arithmetic progression (AP)**, has the same difference between every pair of consecutive terms.

$$a_n-a_{n-1}=d\qquad(n\ge2)$$

::: {.split}
::: {.column-block}
<h3>First term</h3>

$$a_1=a$$

:::
::: {.column-block}
<h3>Recursive rule</h3>

$$a_n=a_{n-1}+d\quad(n\ge2)$$

:::

:::

$$d>0:\ \text{increasing}\qquad d<0:\ \text{decreasing}\qquad d=0:\ \text{constant}$$

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet pp. 10–11 · Arithmetic progression and common difference</p>

::: notes

Use later term minus earlier term consistently. The common difference d is any real constant, including zero or a negative value. The formula applies for every permitted n≥2; for a finite AP it stops at the final index.

:::
